assets.name: Foxleigh Mansion
assets.kind: Lost building · house of the first boys and teachers
assets.summary: The Old House as it stood c.1873–1914: the c.1850 brick Gothic Revival villa, its c.1860s frame addition, the 1873 Trustees' Extension and the rear service range. Burned 30 July 1914.

placement.detail: MZ.Human on site, 3 Nov 2026: footprint sketch, memorial pin and porch bearing (front faces 165°). Expect ±5 m and ±5°.

sources.title: "Foxleigh Mansion" — front view
sources.who: McDonogh School, Wilson | Young Archives · published in 150 Stories #38
sources.used: Main elevation evidence. Camera solved from 19 matched points (7.5 px RMS on 1584 px): roof pitch, gables, bargeboards, chimneys, bay window, veranda, sash windows, storey heights.

sources.title: "Foxleigh Estate" — winter view from the 1883 Main Building tower
sources.who: McDonogh School, Wilson | Young Archives · 150 Stories #38
sources.used: Overall massing and the long frame range. Approximate camera fit (18 px RMS), used to check composition, not to measure.

sources.title: "Foxleigh Mansion or Old House in 1873" — first-floor plan
sources.who: Drawn from memory by Jeff MacHamer and Class of 1970 classmates · 150 Stories #38
sources.used: Every footprint. No scale bar: scaled from its two drawn stairs (≈250 mm treads) to 0.093 m per pixel, giving a 15.7 × 9.8 m brick block and a 47 m range. Rooms, fireplaces and rear service wing come from here.

sources.title: 150 Stories No. 38 · "Foxleigh Estate Becomes McDonogh School"
sources.used: Three storeys plus attic and basement in brick; frame addition to the east; 1873 Trustees' Extension with dining hall below; service rooms; the fire of 30 July 1914.

sources.title: On-site footprint sketch, memorial pin and porch bearing
sources.used: Places the model: memorial at 39.3956616, −76.7760450; front porch faces 165° (south, slightly east).

sources.used: Location of the memorial between Finney Quad and Rollins Hall; the memorial falls inside the Trustees' Extension footprint.

assets.name: Water Tower
assets.kind: Lost structure · gravity-fed every campus building
assets.stats: ≈31.5 m to the top · 9.4 m across the base · tank and legs are placeholder geometry
assets.summary: Built beside Farm Road after the Allan Building was finished. A waterwheel in the pump house on the Gwynns Falls mill race lifted 30,000–40,000 gallons a day to its tank. Taken down in June 1987 after the school moved to city water. The tank and leg design shown is a stand-in until an archive photograph turns up; only the location is confirmed.

placement.detail: 1938 US Coast & Geodetic Survey position agrees within 4 m with MZ.Human's GPS on the surviving south footing (4 Nov 2026). Heading not yet measured.

sources.title: NGS datasheet JV6036 · "McDonogh School tank", intersection station, 1938
sources.who: US Coast & Geodetic Survey / National Geodetic Survey
sources.used: Identifies the tank as a 1938 survey target.

sources.title: NGS datasheets JV6031 (PENNIMAN) and JV6034 (MT WILSON)
sources.used: Survey azimuths from two stations to the tank, intersected to fix its position: 39.3959101, −76.7744983.

sources.title: USGS Reisterstown quadrangle, 1944 and 1953
sources.used: 1944 labels "USC&GS TANK 1938"; 1953 labels "Water". Confirms the tank in the same place.

sources.title: 150 Stories No. 19 · Pump House
sources.used: Built next to Farm Road after Allan Building; fed every building by gravity; the waterwheel ran at 13 rpm for 30–40k gallons a day (Steve Simmers '70); removed June 1987; stood near today's boarder lot.

sources.title: On-site GPS and photographs of the surviving footings
sources.used: Standing on the south footing (square concrete pad ~1 m, chamfered, anchor-bolt hole): 39.3959188, −76.7744518, ±9.5 m — 4 m from the 1938 position. A second slab with bolt stubs lies under the spruce by the soccer field.

sources.title: USGS 3DEP lidar MD_4County_D24, Dec 2024
sources.used: Ground height at the tank centre: 161.4 m.
